$comment: THE CEILINGS, IN ONE PLACE, EACH WITH THE READING IT RESTS ON.
Three readers disagreed about the renderer at 0.17.0 and none of them knew it: the release's
memory gate read 1 048 576 kB, the kit's perf headline guard read the same literal, and the
product declares 1 536 000 kB to itself in apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/vitals.rs. A candidate
was measured RED against a ceiling 68% of the contract the app ships with, and the engine's
own numbers lived as prose in the performance notes where no gate could read them.
So: one table, surface x size class -> ceiling in kB, every ceiling citing the measurement it
rests on by document and date. A ceiling with no reading is not a ceiling — it is null, with
the state that says why, and no gate may read it. test/perf-budgets.test.ts asserts the
shape, asserts the performance notes against this file, and censuses the repository for literals
that should be reading it.
2026-09-15: the renderer's line is three numbers per rig — floor, loaded-undriven, driven — each
naming its drive and its load, because two honest instruments read one binary 367 MB apart and the
largest term was how far the app had been driven. The one-number steady line is retired to history.
The surface's own $comment carries the rule.

$comment: THE RENDERER LINE IS THREE NUMBERS PER RIG, NEVER ONE, AND EACH NAMES ITS DRIVE AND ITS LOAD.
Two honest instruments read the SAME binary on the SAME rig corpus 367 MB apart, and
the largest term in that gap was how far the app had been driven — which no ceiling named. On one
machine, one binary and one mailbox the renderer read 736 828 kB driven through nothing, 850 740
after 30 folder switches and 1 095 148 after 30 switches and 20 searches. A ceiling keyed on the
mailbox passes and fails the same install.
So a renderer row is one of three states of use:
1. FLOOR               — an empty mailbox, freshly relaunched, driven through nothing. Ruled in
PSS: ~200 MB of the floor is file-backed WebKit/GTK/Mesa text that RSS
counts again in the shell and the network process, so an RSS floor is
partly a ceiling on how many times the same pages are counted.
2. LOADED, UNDRIVEN    — a stated corpus, freshly relaunched and settled, driven through
nothing. LOADED minus FLOOR is the per-message allowance.
3. DRIVEN              — after a NAMED drive: 30 folder switches, then 20 searches. This is the
state a person's app is in after ten minutes, and the one a ceiling has
to bound.
Two rules follow from the readings rather than from taste:
· THE SOFTWARE-RASTERISER CLASS IS STATED AND EXCLUDED across distributions. 61 628 kB of the
difference between two honest readings was Mesa's VERSION. A ceiling that includes it measures
the distribution, not the app. Its own row is `rasteriser-class-linux`.
· A FIGURE WITHOUT ITS DRIVE AND ITS LOAD IS NOT A FIGURE. Every row here carries both, `unread`
with the reason where the reading does not have one, and the reader refuses to print a number
for a row that carries neither.
For 0.19.1 each ceiling IS the 0.19.0 reading at that drive — a no-regression line. The freeze
compares a candidate's three numbers at the SAME drive against these, and a regression in any of
the three blocks. Goals are aspirational and printed apart under `goalKb`/`goalState`; where no
goal has been ruled the row says `owed` rather than borrowing the retired one.

$comment: DURATIONS IN MILLISECONDS, kept apart from the kB memory surfaces above so a reader never
budgets a millisecond figure against a kilobyte ceiling.
EVERY ENTRY HERE CARRIES ITS SHAPE AND ITS ORIGIN, and `test/perf-budgets.test.ts` refuses a
malformed one. Before 2026-09-16 this block lived outside `surfaces`, which that test iterates,
so a latency entry could ship with no origin, no state and no arm and nothing would say - which
is how seven budgets came to be quoted with no measurement behind any of them
(two rows of the project's ledger).
The shape, and each rule's reason:
· `what`   - what is being timed. A number with no subject is not a budget.
· `state`  - `measured` (a run has read this and the number rests on it) or `no-origin-yet`
(the number is a line somebody wrote and nothing has been measured at it).
· `arm`    - `decides` (a run over it is RED) or `records` (printed, reddens nothing). A
`no-origin-yet` entry may only RECORD: an arm that reddens a build against a
number nobody measured is the failure this table exists to remove.
· `origin` - the run the number came from, or `null` under `no-origin-yet`. Never absent.
· p95/p99 both where the budget is a percentile pair, and p99 is never below p95.
· `readings` may exist under `no-origin-yet` and do NOT promote it: a reading of how long
something takes is not a measurement of what it is allowed to take.

MEASURED 2026-09-16: a SIXTH reader, and it APPLIES ten budgets of its own - a renderer peak, the engine's 450 MB, and the eight latency and throughput lines, which are this table's numbers copied. contested.whyNotGenerated: STRUCTURAL, not an oversight: this file is PUBLISHED (scripts/perf-smoke-check.mjs is a payload row) and this table is not, so the check cannot read it at runtime in the mirror's CI - which is why it already treats an unreadable table as an unruled ceiling rather than a failure. Folding it needs either a generated block inside the published file or a payload row for a generated sibling, and scripts/lib/ is the private toolchain it may not import from. What HAS been done: the census literals now include its two memory spellings, so this reader is visible and a SEVENTH cannot arrive quietly, and its one table read (the derivation p95) reads this table's own state word.

the pass runs once per version bump and holds the thread while it does, so that is the
frame it has to fit inside to be invisible. Nothing has been measured AT it - the
figures that exist are 67 ms at the small class, 297 ms at the middle class and 180-480 ms over the rig's full corpus from a
rig, and the shipped 0.19.0 read a median of 8 ms on the Omarchy guest. The first green
run is what would give it an origin as a budget.

vars.name: PERF_SYNC_MSG_PER_S
note: 60 msg/s is 2.3x the released build, and the arm is readable the moment first_sync_finished lands.

vars.name: PERF_SYNC_UI_STALL_MS
note: NO-ORIGIN-YET: no run has measured a UI stall during a sync at all.

sections.title: the sample shape every reader insists on
note: A 60-second window read the incident's renderer as FALLING while the session
quadrupled. PERF_MIN_SPAN_S is the WINDOW EVERY CELL NEEDS, not a plan: a reader
refuses a shorter one by name and names this line, and --min-span moves it for a reason
that belongs in the run's notes.

consts.name: RENDERER_BUDGET_KB
note: The product's own declared renderer ceiling, written into every renderer_vitals line.
It used to be a literal here, and it was a FOURTH reader of a number three other readers
already disagreed about - the one a person actually sees in the log. It reads the ruled
ceiling now, which sits BELOW what the shell used to promise itself, so the app no longer
declares more headroom than its gate allows. A LOG LINE, never a limit: the shell does not
kill the window it is reporting on.
